frequency_question: How often has the U.S. Federal Reserve increased the countercyclical capital buffer above 0% across comparable historical regulatory review windows?
membership_rule: Includes all U.S. Federal Reserve policy decision cycles regarding the CCyB since the framework's inception where economic conditions were non-recessionary. Excludes foreign central banks and crisis intervention periods where emergency loosening occurred.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 named annual review cycles; covers the entirety of the operational history of the framework in the US.
known_gaps: The framework has existed for a relatively short historical duration, meaning all observations are drawn from the post-GFC era.
skeleton: Annual policy review cycles since the formal establishment of the CCyB framework in the US.
multiplier: 7 annual observation windows with 0 positive adjustments above 0%.
validity_reason: Regulatory frameworks and institutional inertia around macroprudential buffers change slowly over multi-year horizons.
